subject.title: [Enhancement] Prepared Statement Compilation Overhead in executeCompiledSqliteQuerySync (Kysely Sync Facade)

question: Should this newly rewritten, unreleased facade gain a custom bounded statement cache before representative OpenClaw benchmarks demonstrate a material benefit?
rationale: Source inspection proves repeated preparation but cannot determine the performance threshold that justifies permanent cache, eviction, and lifecycle complexity in a stable gateway surface.

options.title: Benchmark before caching
options.body: Measure representative SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE workloads and allocations on Node 22 and Node 24, approving a bounded cache only for a material improvement.

options.title: Approve bounded cache now
options.body: Extend the existing per-database clear contract immediately with a small bounded cache and eager, iterator, eviction, and close-order tests.

options.title: Keep current simplicity
options.body: Retain per-call preparation unless production profiling later identifies this facade as a meaningful bottleneck.

recommendation.title: Benchmark before caching
recommendation.body: Measure representative SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE workloads and allocations on Node 22 and Node 24, approving a bounded cache only for a material improvement.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cache, execution, iterator, and test contracts all originate in Vincent Koc's July 12 facade rewrite.
